1. [Home](https://studyandwork.yesmilano.it/en)
2. [Work](https://studyandwork.yesmilano.it/en/work)
3. [Getting Started Guide](https://studyandwork.yesmilano.it/en/work/getting-started-guide)
4. Learn Italian

_Impara l'italiano a Milano!_

If you come to Milan as an international student enrolled in an English-language program, you’ll find it easy to get around and study without speaking Italian. Still, learning the local language is a great opportunity to **appreciate the Milanese lifestyle** and **better integrate into the professional environment**. Speaking Italian can help you connect more naturally with colleagues, understand workplace culture, and navigate everyday interactions.

- [MUNICIPALITY OF MILANO LANGUAGE COURSES](https://studyandwork.yesmilano.it/en/work/getting-started-guide/learn-italian#blocco-redazionale-tab-12500)
- [AT YOUR UNIVERSITY / ACADEMY](https://studyandwork.yesmilano.it/en/work/getting-started-guide/learn-italian#blocco-redazionale-tab-12501)
- [FREE ITALIAN COURSES AT CPIA](https://studyandwork.yesmilano.it/en/work/getting-started-guide/learn-italian#blocco-redazionale-tab-12502)
- [CONVERSATION FOR IMPROVING YOUR ITALIAN](https://studyandwork.yesmilano.it/en/work/getting-started-guide/learn-italian#blocco-redazionale-tab-12508)

### MUNICIPALITY OF MILANO LANGUAGE COURSES

The City of Milano offers high-quality, affordable Italian language courses for adults (18+), from absolute beginners (A1) to advanced level (C2). These courses are heavily subsidised by the Municipality to support non-Italian residents living and working in Milan. You can look for "Italiano per Stranieri" on the [dedicated website](https://formami.comune.milano.it/lingue/).

#### 📍 Where Are the Courses Held?

Courses take place at the following municipal centres:

- **Via Fleming 15** – Tel. 02 884 41458, [plo.fleming@comune.milano.it](mailto:plo.pepe@comune.milano.it)
- **Viale Murillo 17** – Tel. 02 884 40136 / 4, [plo.murillo@comune.milano.it](mailto:plo.murillo@comune.milano.it)
- **Via Pepe 40** – Tel. 02 884 48421, [plo.pepe@comune.milano.it](mailto:plo.pepe@comune.milano.it)
- **Corso XXII Marzo 59/a** – Tel. 02 884 65554 / 5, [plo.XXIIMarzo@comune.milano.it](mailto:plo.XXIIMarzo@comune.milano.it)

If you are unsure which centre to choose, you may contact the one closest to your home.

#### 📅 When Do Courses Start?

Courses run throughout the year, except during the summer months (June, July and August).

Most courses begin:

- End of September / beginning of October
- February
- April

Exact dates are published on the official website.

#### 🕒 Course Structure & Schedule

Each course is organised in **60-hour modules**.

The contribution you will pay is **109 euros** per module. You can pay by credit or debit card at the school

or at a Post Office using the payment slip provided by the Centre. Cash is not accepted.

Please note: fees are **not refundable**, except if the course is cancelled by the school.

Different levels (A1, A2, B1, etc.) courses and schedules are available:

- _Mono Settimanale_ lessons are once a week;
- _Bisettimanale_ lessons are twice a week;
- _Intensivo_ means that you will take class three times a week;
- _Classe+online_ when one class is in person and the other online.




#### 👤 Who Can Enrol?


You must:

- Be at least 18 years old
- Know the Latin alphabet



You must bring:

- Valid passport or ID
- For non-EU citizens: valid Permesso di Soggiorno (or receipt of application/visa)
- Codice Fiscale (if already issued)
- Documents must be valid for the entire duration of the course.

If you attend at least **75%** of the course you will be able to take a final test and access the **priority lane** in signing up for the following modules.

#### 🔵 How to Enrol – Step by Step

#### If You Have NEVER Studied Italian (Absolute Beginner – A1):

1. Go to:

[http://formami.comune.milano.it/area-riservata](http://formami.comune.milano.it/area-riservata)
2. Create your personal account.
3. Wait for the confirmation email (check spam folder).
4. Log in and click **“Prenotazioni”**.
5. Book an appointment at your chosen school to enrol.



Alternatively, you may contact the school directly by phone to book the appointment.


➡ Absolute beginners usually do **not** need a written test.

A short interview with the teacher is sufficient.

#### If You HAVE Studied Italian Before:

You must take a **free placement test** before enrolling.

1. Register at:

[http://formami.comune.milano.it/area-riservata](http://formami.comune.milano.it/area-riservata)
2. Wait for email confirmation.
3. Log in and click:

**“Prenotazioni” → TEST ITALIANO**
4. Choose: The school (Sede), Available date and Available time
5. Attend the test in person on the selected date.


After your level is determined, you will complete enrolment and payment.

⚠️ If no dates are available, registration is temporarily closed.

Contact the school directly to ask when new booking slots will open.

#### 📚 Additional Important Information & Notes

- **Classes:** minimum 10 students, maximum 18
- Italian is spoken from the first lesson
- There are 10 levels (A1 to C2 – CEFR framework)
- At the end of each level, there is a final test
- Certificates of enrolment and attendance are available upon request
- These courses **do not qualify** for a student stay permit (minimum 20 hours per week required).
- Certificates issued by these centres **cannot** be used to request a long-term residence permit.
- CILS exam sessions are available for higher levels (held at Viale Murillo 17).



[**BOOK THE LANGUAGE TEST AND ENROLL**](https://formami.comune.milano.it/prenotazione-test/)


### AT YOUR UNIVERSITY / ACADEMY

Most of the universities and academies in Milano offer Italian language classes for their students, in addition to that, many other language schools are present in the city.

Some courses prepare you for the official Italian as a Foreign Language Certificate (there are four official certifications: CILS, CELI, [CERT.IT](http://cert.it/), PLIDA) that some universities might require you to get.

Inquire at your University/Academy International office or welcome desk

The municipality of Milano created the website [**milano.italianostranieri.org**](https://milano.italianostranieri.org/en/#search_row_target). It hosts a comprehensive database of Italian language courses offered in the city.

Please note: the website is no longer updated, but it is still useful to get the names of the Italian language schools. We suggest you get in contact with the single institutes to ask for further information.

- [**SEARCH FOR ITALIAN LANGUAGE COURSES IN MILANO**](http://milano.italianostranieri.org/en/)

### FREE ITALIAN COURSES AT CPIA

CPIA stands for **Centro Provinciale per l’Istruzione degli Adulti** (Provincial Centre for Adult Education).

CPIA schools are **public state schools**, established by the Italian Ministry of Education, offering **free adult education courses**, including Italian language courses for foreigners.

These schools support personal, cultural and professional development for adults living in Italy.

#### 📍 **CPIA Schools in Milan**

CPIA Milano has several branches across the city: look them up [here](http://milano.italianostranieri.org/it/pages/corsi-di-italiano-gratuiti-nelle-scuola-pubbliche-di-milano)

- CPIA Via Pontano
- CPIA Via Heine
- CPIA Via Colletta
- CPIA Viale Zara
- CPIA Via Scrosati
- CPIA Via Satta
- CPIA Viale Campania


You can choose the branch closest to your residence.

#### 👤 **Who Can Enrol?**

You can enrol if:

- You are **16 years old or older**
- You are an Italian or foreign citizen
- If you are a foreign citizen, you must have a **valid residence permit**


#### 📚 What Courses Are Offered?

CPIA offers:

1. **Italian Language Courses (Italian L2)**

For foreigners who want to: Learn Italian from beginner to advanced level, improve integration in Italy and prepare for language certification.

2. **Middle School Diploma (Licenza Media):** Courses to obtain the Italian lower secondary school diploma.
3. **Other Courses** such as Foreign language courses or basic computer skills courses.


All teachers are qualified Ministry of Education teachers specialised in adult education.

At the end of Italian language courses, and after passing the final test, CPIA issues a: **Certificate of Italian Language Competence (L2)**(Attestato di competenza di lingua italiana)

#### 🔵 **How to Enrol – Step by Step**

Enrolment procedures may vary slightly between branches, but generally follow these steps:

1. **Choose Your CPIA Branch:** Select the school closest to your residence.
2. **Contact the School Directly**

Visit the website of the chosen CPIA branch or contact the school office by:

- Email
- Telephone
- In person during office hours

Ask:

- When enrolment is open
- Which documents are required
- Available course levels and schedules

⚠️ Registration is not open all year. It usually opens before the start of each academic term.

3. **Prepare Required Documents**

Typically you will need:

- Valid ID or passport
- Valid residence permit (for non-EU citizens)
- Codice Fiscale (if available)

Some schools may ask for:

- Proof of residence/domicile
- Passport photos


4. **Placement Test** (If Required)

If you have studied Italian before, you may need to take a **free placement test** to determine your level.

5. **Complete Registration**

Once your level is confirmed, you will finalise your enrolment at the school office.

CPIA Italian language courses are generally **free**.

Some small administrative fees may apply depending on the course.

#### 📝 **Important to Know**

- Courses follow the Italian public school calendar.
- Attendance is important to access final exams and certification.
- CPIA certificates may be useful for integration and residence procedures, depending on the level.



[**CPIA IN MILANO**](https://milano.italianostranieri.org/it/post/tutte-le-sedi-del-cpia-milano-ex-ctp-aggiornate-iscrivetevi-ai-corsi-di-italiano-della-scuola-pubblica)


### CONVERSATION FOR IMPROVING YOUR ITALIAN

If you already speak some Italian and are looking for a fun and simple approach for improving your Italian without spending money and sitting further in a classroom, organizations such as ESN organize language exchange programs where you can pair up with local people and have informal chats. You might even make friends along the way!

ESN is one of the main international students associations. Its groups in Milano Universities have Tandem one-to-one conversation programs. They even have an app for that. Get in touch with them!

### Dichiarazioni Tari per le utenze domestiche

Il calcolo Tari è determinato dalla situazione abitativa/immobiliare.

Ogni cambiamento della situazione abitativa incide sulla tariffa Tari e richiede la presentazione della dichiarazione di nuova occupazione, di cessazione di occupazione, di variazione del numero di occupanti non residenti o di metratura.
